title: 郡斋雨中与诸文士燕集
title_en: A Feast with Scholars at My Office on a Rainy Day
author: 韦应物

text_note.zh: 通行本（如《唐诗三百首》）末句作“岂曰财赋强”，这里的底本作“财赋疆”。底本的“慙”“覩”是“惭”“睹”的异体字，这里用通行写法。题目中的“燕”同“宴”。
text_note.en: Common editions, such as the Three Hundred Tang Poems, end with cai fu qiang (rich in money and taxes); the source text has a different last character, jiang. The source also uses older variant forms of two characters, written here in their usual forms. In the title, the character yan means a feast.

readings.zh: “居处”在这里是名词，指住的地方、所处的地位，读 chù。一说读 chǔ。
readings.en: Here ju chu is a noun, the place one lives or the position one holds, so it is read chù. Some read it chǔ.

readings.zh: 这里读 shǔ，意思是正赶上、属于。
readings.en: Here it is read shǔ, meaning to happen to fall in.

readings.zh: 这里读 qiáng，意思是强盛、多。
readings.en: Here it is read qiáng, meaning strong or plentiful.

glosses.en: bīng wèi: soldiers on guard.

glosses.zh: 森画戟：排列着很多画戟。森，排得密密的。画戟，有彩色装饰的戟，唐代高官门前才能摆。
glosses.en: sēn huà jǐ: rows of painted halberds. Sēn means standing thick together. Painted halberds were set outside the gates of high officials in the Tang.
yàn qǐn: the inner rooms where one rests.

glosses.zh: 凝清香：屋里点的香，香气聚着不散。
glosses.en: níng qīng xiāng: the scent of burning incense hangs in the air.

glosses.zh: 海上：苏州靠近大海，风雨从海上吹来。
glosses.en: hǎi shàng: from the sea. Suzhou is near the sea, so the wind and rain come from there.
xiāo yáo: free and easy.
chí gé: a pavilion by a pond.
fán kē: restlessness and sickness. Kē means illness.
jiā bīn: honoured guests.

glosses.zh: 居处崇：住处高大，地位高。
glosses.en: jū chù chóng: living in a grand place, holding a high post.

glosses.zh: 斯民康：这里的百姓过上安康的日子。斯，这。
glosses.en: sī mín kāng: the people here living in peace and comfort. Sī means this.

glosses.zh: 理会是非遣：明白了道理，争是争非的念头就放下了。遣，丢开。
glosses.en: lǐ huì shì fēi qiǎn: once you understand the way of things, you let go of arguing over right and wrong. Qiǎn means to send away.

glosses.zh: 性达形迹忘：心胸开阔，就忘了身份和礼节的拘束。
glosses.en: xìng dá xíng jì wàng: with an open heart, you forget rank and stiff manners.
xiān féi: fish and meat.

glosses.zh: 时禁：当时禁止宰杀牲畜的规定。
glosses.en: shí jìn: a rule of the season that forbade killing animals for food.

glosses.zh: 幸见尝：希望大家尝一尝。见，表示对我。
glosses.en: xìng jiàn cháng: I hope you will taste them. Jiàn here shows the guests are doing the host a favour.
fǔ: to bow the head.
yǎng: to raise the head.
líng: to listen.

glosses.zh: 金玉章：像金子玉石一样珍贵的诗文，指客人们作的诗。
glosses.en: jīn yù zhāng: writings as precious as gold and jade, meaning the guests' poems.
líng fēng xiáng: to fly on the wind.
wú zhōng: the Suzhou area.

glosses.zh: 盛文史：文章和学问很兴盛。
glosses.en: shèng wén shǐ: rich in writing and learning.

glosses.zh: 群彦：一群有才华的人。彦，有才德的人。
glosses.en: qún yàn: a crowd of talented people. Yàn means a gifted person.

glosses.zh: 汪洋：像大海一样广阔，形容人才多、文采盛。
glosses.en: wāng yáng: as wide as the sea, meaning many talents and rich writing.
dà fān: a large prefecture.
cái fù qiáng: rich in money and taxes.

translation.zh: 门口守卫的士兵排列着彩绘的画戟，
translation.en: At the gate, guards stand among rows of painted halberds.

translation.zh: 休息的内室里聚着清清的香气。
translation.en: In the inner rooms, a clear scent of incense hangs in the air.

translation.zh: 海上吹来了风雨，
translation.en: Wind and rain have come in from the sea,

translation.zh: 池边楼阁里凉爽，人也自在。
translation.en: and the pavilion by the pond is cool and easy.

translation.zh: 最近烦闷和病痛刚刚消散，
translation.en: My restlessness and sickness have lately cleared,

translation.zh: 尊贵的客人又坐满了大堂。
translation.en: and honoured guests fill the hall once more.

translation.zh: 我惭愧自己身居高位，
translation.en: I am ashamed to hold so high a post

translation.zh: 却还没看到百姓过上安康的日子。
translation.en: while I have not yet seen the people here live in comfort.

translation.zh: 懂了道理，就放下了是是非非，
translation.en: Understanding the way of things, I let go of right and wrong;

translation.zh: 心胸开阔，就忘了身份和拘束。
translation.en: with an open heart, I forget rank and stiff manners.

translation.zh: 鱼肉正赶上时令禁止，
translation.en: Fish and meat are forbidden this season,

translation.zh: 只有蔬菜水果，希望大家尝一尝。
translation.en: so I hope you will taste the vegetables and fruit.

translation.zh: 低头喝下一杯酒，
translation.en: I bow my head and drink a cup of wine,

translation.zh: 抬头听大家吟诵金玉般的好诗。
translation.en: then raise it to hear poems as precious as gold and jade.

translation.zh: 精神愉快，身体也觉得轻了，
translation.en: My spirit is glad and my body feels light,

translation.zh: 真想乘着风飞上天去。
translation.en: and I wish I could ride the wind and fly.

translation.zh: 苏州一带文章学问兴盛，
translation.en: The Suzhou region is rich in writing and learning,

translation.zh: 今天的人才像大海一样多。
translation.en: and today its talents are as many as the sea.

translation.zh: 这才知道，这个大州
translation.en: Now I know that this great prefecture

translation.zh: 哪里只是财富赋税多呢！
translation.en: is not only rich in money and taxes!

background.zh: 韦应物晚年做过苏州刺史，也就是苏州的长官。这首诗一般认为是他在苏州任上时写的，大约在唐德宗贞元年间。一个下雨的日子，他在官府里请当地的文人们吃饭、作诗。诗里写了宴会的清凉和快乐，也写了他做官的惭愧，最后称赞苏州人才多。
background.en: Late in life, Wei Yingwu served as governor of Suzhou. This poem is usually thought to have been written there, during the Zhenyuan years of Emperor Dezong. On a rainy day he invited the local scholars to his office for food and poems. The poem shows the cool, happy feast and his shame as an official, and ends by praising how many talented people Suzhou has.

author_note.zh: 韦应物（约737—约792），唐代诗人。他年轻时在宫里当侍卫，很任性，后来发愤读书，做过滁州、江州、苏州的刺史，人称“韦苏州”。他的诗清淡自然，常常关心百姓，比如“邑有流亡愧俸钱”。这首诗里“自惭居处崇，未睹斯民康”也是同样的心情。
author_note.en: Wei Yingwu (about 737–about 792) was a Tang poet. As a young man he was a reckless palace guard. Later he studied hard and became governor of Chuzhou, Jiangzhou and Suzhou, so people called him Wei Suzhou. His poems are plain and natural, and he often cared about ordinary people. He once wrote that he felt ashamed of his pay while people in his county had fled their homes. The line here about his high post and the people's hardship shows the same feeling.

appreciation.zh: 开头两句很有名：门外是排排画戟，威严庄重；屋里却是一缕清香，安静高雅。接着海上风雨吹来，楼阁变得凉爽，病也好了，客人坐满一堂。主人没有得意，反而惭愧自己地位高，百姓却还没过上好日子。他放下是非，忘掉身份，用蔬菜水果招待客人，一边喝酒，一边听大家吟诗，高兴得想乘风飞起来。最后他感叹：苏州的宝贵不只是钱多，更是人才多。整首诗清凉、雅致，又有一颗关心百姓的心。
appreciation.en: The opening two lines are famous. Outside the gate stand rows of painted halberds, stern and grand. Inside there is only a thread of clear incense, quiet and refined. Then wind and rain blow in from the sea, the pavilion turns cool, his illness has passed, and guests fill the hall. The host is not proud. Instead he feels ashamed that his post is so high while the people still live hard lives. He lets go of right and wrong and forgets his rank. He serves vegetables and fruit, drinks wine and listens to poems, so happy he wants to fly on the wind. At the end he says what makes Suzhou precious is not its money but its talented people. The poem is cool and graceful, with a heart that cares for ordinary people.
